bug_semantics: TemplateContext.LimitToString bounded only one ObjectToString conversion, not the cumulative rendered template. TemplateContext.Write(SourceSpan, object) converts each rendered expression through a fresh top-level ObjectToString call; ObjectToString resets _currentToStringLength whenever _objectToStringLevel is zero; and StringBuilderOutput.Write appends every resulting chunk without a cumulative cap. A template can therefore make a 1,048,575-character string, render it in each of the default 1000 loop iterations, pass the 1,048,576-character per-call limit every time, and accumulate roughly 1 GB in the output StringBuilder until the host process runs out of memory.
flaw_origin: Commit b858377886c35bfedb2768de9b057377909c2e95 (Add TemplateContext.LimitToString) introduced the vulnerable safety mechanism: it added _currentToStringLength and reset it to zero at every top-level ObjectToString call, while leaving the already-existing output sink cumulative-unbounded. The older unconditional StringBuilderOutput append is a precondition, but b858377886c35bfedb2768de9b057377909c2e95 is the smallest commit that created the advisory's LimitToString-bypass combination; b5ac4bf30459fdc76964e3f751e16f7e96079ea7 later changed the default LimitToString from disabled to 1,048,576 and made the bypass present under default 6.6.0 settings rather than introducing the reset.
ai_marker: absent — BIC commit object has no AI author/co-author/Generated-with marker; see evidence
evidence: The first-party repository advisory https://github.com/scriban/scriban/security/advisories/GHSA-m2p3-hwv5-xpqw describes the exact flow Write(SourceSpan, object) -> ObjectToString, the top-level _currentToStringLength reset, unconditional StringBuilderOutput append, the near-1-MB string repeated 1000 times, affected versions <= 6.6.0, and patched version 7.0.0. The bundle maps that first-party advisory to CVE-2026-74786 / GHSA-w7vg-5328-m33q.

In the assigned clone, `git show b858377886c35bfedb2768de9b057377909c2e95 -- src/Scriban/TemplateContext.Helpers.cs src/Scriban/TemplateContext.cs` shows one focused non-merge commit adding LimitToString, _currentToStringLength, and exactly `if (_objectToStringLevel == 0) { _currentToStringLength = 0; }`; it initializes LimitToString to 0 and does not add cumulative accounting to the output path.

Both required history searches converge on the same BIC: `git log --all --reverse -S'_currentToStringLength' -- src/Scriban/TemplateContext.Helpers.cs src/Scriban/TemplateContext.cs` returns b858377886c35bfedb2768de9b057377909c2e95 as the first addition, and `git log b858377886c35bfedb2768de9b057377909c2e95 -L 85,88:src/Scriban/TemplateContext.Helpers.cs` attributes the entire four-line top-level reset to that commit.

Direct parent verification: `git cat-file commit b858377886c35bfedb2768de9b057377909c2e95` names sole parent d4d64f8f15df9683ec0d51d4906edc4b3cef5ff5. `git show d4d64f8f15df9683ec0d51d4906edc4b3cef5ff5:src/Scriban/TemplateContext.Helpers.cs` has _objectToStringLevel but has neither _currentToStringLength nor LimitToString nor the reset; ObjectToString simply increments the nesting level and returns ObjectToStringImpl. Thus the immediate parent lacks the advisory-specific per-call limit/reset mechanism.

The cumulative-unbounded sink predates the BIC: `git log --all --reverse -S'Builder.Append(text, offset, count)' -- src/Scriban/Runtime/StringBuilderOutput.cs` traces the synchronous append to bfa7fc100ca6d337bd61247319080f91767f462a (2017), while `git show 6.6.0:src/Scriban/Runtime/StringBuilderOutput.cs` confirms both Write and WriteAsync append directly with no total-output check in the last affected release.

Default-exploitability boundary: `git show b5ac4bf30459fdc76964e3f751e16f7e96079ea7` identifies `Add limits for default safety`, which changes the TemplateContext LimitToString default to 1,048,576 without removing b858377886c35bfedb2768de9b057377909c2e95's per-call reset. `git rev-parse 6.6.0^{}` resolves the annotated 6.6.0 tag to b5ac4bf30459fdc76964e3f751e16f7e96079ea7.

Closing fix: `git show 98563216488161a9edeba6c37c7cf82c98319c9b -- src/Scriban/TemplateContext.cs src/Scriban/TemplateContext.Helpers.cs` adds _currentOutputLength, routes output and indentation chunks through WriteOutputChunk/GetAllowedOutputCount, emits one ellipsis after truncation, and resets cumulative tracking in TemplateContext.Reset. Its sole parent is 8180fb6cd1f6c2727c99f8f5a745a0b991b06cfc, so this is the direct source fix rather than a release merge or backport.

Release boundary: `git tag --contains 98563216488161a9edeba6c37c7cf82c98319c9b --sort=version:refname` starts at 7.0.0 and contains no 6.x tag; `git rev-parse 6.6.0^{} 7.0.0^{}` resolves the last affected and first patched releases to b5ac4bf30459fdc76964e3f751e16f7e96079ea7 and 25d148a104dd4d679a1a1932442616599e003c2f respectively.

BIC-only AI check: `git cat-file commit b858377886c35bfedb2768de9b057377909c2e95` shows author and committer Alexandre Mutel <alexandre_mutel@live.com>, subject `Add TemplateContext.LimitToString`, no message body, no Co-authored-by/Generated-with or other AI trailer, and no bot identity. The Copilot co-author trailer on the 2026 fix commit is deliberately excluded because the protocol permits AI evidence only from the BIC commit object.
reasoning: The advisory is specifically a bypass of LimitToString caused by per-conversion state, not merely the general fact that an output StringBuilder can grow. The direct sink existed earlier, but the vulnerable safety invariant became expressible and false when b858377886c35bfedb2768de9b057377909c2e95 added a length counter that is reset at every top-level conversion. Its parent directly lacks that mechanism, and -S plus -L both establish that b858377886c35bfedb2768de9b057377909c2e95 wrote the decisive lines; it is an ordinary single-parent commit, so there is no squash to decompose. The later b5ac4bf30459fdc76964e3f751e16f7e96079ea7 default change explains why the published 6.6.0 PoC works with untouched defaults but is not the first introduction. The direct fix 98563216488161a9edeba6c37c7cf82c98319c9b moves enforcement to cumulative writes and first ships in 7.0.0. Since the BIC commit object contains only a human author/committer and no AI marker, the closed causal verdict is NOT_AI; AI attribution on the fix cannot change it.
